natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: The two live symptoms are activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ), and the single most directly targeted lever is shortening onboarding (memory_86), reinforced by the signup-field reduction result (memory_31). I verify those two because they are the ones I am about to act on and they are the oldest/most load-bearing: memory_86 and memory_31 are stated only as directional summaries with no effect sizes, no sample, and no retention follow-through, so I want the original records to confirm the lift was real, durable past week one, and measured on a population resembling today's self-serve base rather than a pre-competitor cohort. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_73 because its numbers are already specific enough to reject on: 40% off bought signup +31% and revenue +18% at the cost of retention -12%, which is exactly the trade that destroys sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and matching the competitor on price would compound that by anchoring the segment lower and attracting the least durable accounts. Referral incentive (memory_57) is a real option but it works on established customers and does nothing for the two metrics actually bleeding; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the one under attack. Uncertainty I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose sources I cannot fully audit, none carries a confidence interval, and every result predates the competitor launch, so the environment that produced them has changed and prior effect sizes may not replicate. Onboarding work also has a downstream value risk I am flagging explicitly: removing fields and steps can raise completion while lowering lead qualification and downstream fit, so short-term activation gains can mask worse revenue quality later, which is structurally the same failure mode as memory_73. I therefore run this at standard experiment scale with retention and qualified-pipeline as guardrail metrics measured beyond week one, not just completion and activation. If verification shows memory_86 or memory_31 measured only first-week activation with no durability check, I will downgrade to a small guarded test rather than proceed at this scale.
